title_candidates: Before you forward AI output, own the answer
summary: A useful rule for AI-assisted messages: read the draft, verify important claims, then rewrite it for the person receiving it.

primary_source.title: Don't be a meat proxy
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Willison highlights Niklas Gruhn's term for someone who forwards AI-generated material without checking it.
The recommended alternative is to read, understand, and verify an AI response before communicating its substance in your own words.
Rewriting the result yourself shows that you reviewed it and adds human judgment instead of merely passing along machine output.

quote_candidates.text: By all means, prompt AI. But don't just relay the output.

supporting_sources.title: Don't be a meat proxy
key_facts: Gruhn argues that pasted AI output makes the recipient do extra work because they must interpret, check, and adapt a response they did not ask the model to produce.
He recommends understanding and validating the result, then writing the response in your own words.

supporting_sources.title: Does ChatGPT tell the truth?
key_facts: OpenAI says ChatGPT can give incorrect or misleading answers confidently.
Its guidance is to treat AI output as a draft and verify important claims, quotes, data, technical details, and references against reliable sources.

prerequisites: The original question and intended recipient
Independent sources for any important factual claims

steps.instruction: Write the recipient's actual question in one sentence, then read the entire AI draft. Mark every claim or term you cannot explain yourself; if any remain unclear, do not forward the draft.
Open reliable source material and independently confirm any claim that could change the recipient's decision. Remove unsupported claims, and stop if a consequential point remains uncertain.
Ask whether you could answer a follow-up about each remaining claim without reopening the AI transcript. Research or omit anything you cannot defend.
Close the AI output and rewrite the answer for this specific person. Keep only the relevant conclusion, evidence links, and uncertainty; the message should stand alone.
Before sending, confirm the message contains no private material and that you can stand behind it as your response. If either check fails, ask for clarification or send nothing.

risk_flags: The term is intentionally provocative; the article should explain the behavior without labeling the reader.
The guide uses non-sensitive drafts and requires independent verification before sharing consequential claims.
